chapters.title: The King's Food, and the Wisdom God Gave
chapters.html:
Daniel 1

Taken to Babylon

1In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

2The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with some of the vessels of the house of God. He carried them off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.

3Then the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring in some of the sons of Israel, from the royal family and from the nobles:

4young men without any blemish, good-looking, skilled in every kind of wisdom, well informed and quick to understand, with the ability to stand in the king's palace; and he was to teach them the literature and the language of the Chaldeans.

5The king assigned them a daily portion of the king's food and of the wine he drank. They were to be trained for three years, and at the end of that time they were to stand before the king.

6Among them, from the sons of Judah, were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.

7The chief of the eunuchs gave them names: he gave Daniel the name Belteshazzar, Hananiah Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.

Ten Days

8Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king's food or with the wine he drank, and he asked the chief of the eunuchs for permission not to defile himself.

9God gave Daniel kindness and compassion in the sight of the chief of the eunuchs.

10The chief of the eunuchs said to Daniel, "I am afraid of my lord the king, who has assigned your food and your drink. Why should he see your faces more downcast than the young men your own age? You would make my head forfeit to the king."

11Daniel said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah,

12"Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given vegetables to eat and water to drink.

13Then look at our appearance and the appearance of the young men who eat the king's food, and deal with your servants by what you see."

14He listened to them in this matter and tested them for ten days.

15At the end of ten days their appearance was better, and they were fatter of flesh than all the young men who ate the king's food.

16So the steward would take away their food and the wine they were to drink, and give them vegetables.

Ten Times Wiser

17To these four young men God gave knowledge and skill in all literature and wisdom, and Daniel understood visions and dreams of every kind.

18At the end of the time the king had set for them to be brought in, the chief of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.

19The king spoke with them, and among them all no one was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah. So they stood before the king.

20In every matter of wisdom and understanding that the king asked them about, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his whole kingdom.

21Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.

Notes

  • v1 "In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim" — Kings tells it in one line: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years (2 Kings 24:1). Chronicles adds the vessels: Nebuchadnezzar also brought some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his temple in Babylon (2 Chronicles 36:7). Jeremiah counts the fourth year of Jehoiakim… which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar (Jeremiah 25:1; 46:2), a year later than Daniel's date. Neither book refers to the other's count.

  • v2 "the land of Shinar" — the old name of Babylonia, the plain of the tower: they found a valley in the land of Shinar, and they settled there (Genesis 11:2). The vessels of the house of God go into the house of Nebuchadnezzar's god. They come out again in 5:2–4.

  • vv2, 9, 17 "gave" — natan, with God as the one who gives each time: the Lord gave Jehoiakim into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, God gave Daniel kindness and compassion, God gave the four knowledge. The defeat, the favor and the wisdom all come from the same hand. In v9 the words are those of Solomon's prayer for Israel in exile, grant them compassion before their captors (1 Kings 8:50), natan… le-rachamim lifnei. The Lord in v2 is Adonai; the name YHWH appears in Daniel only in chapter 9.

  • vv3–4 "the chief of his eunuchs… from the royal family" — sarisim, the word of Isaiah's warning to Hezekiah: Some of your sons, who will come from you… shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon (Isaiah 39:7; 2 Kings 20:18). Here young men of the royal family are chosen to stand in the king's palace, heikhal, the same word. Saris can also mean a court officer: Potiphar, who had a wife, is an officer of Pharaoh (Genesis 39:1). The chapter does not say whether the four were made eunuchs. The Greek has archieunouchos, chief eunuch. Choice in the report.

  • vv6–8 the names — each Hebrew name carries God's. Daniel is dan, judge, with El, God (Rachel's God has judged me, Genesis 30:6); Mishael also ends in El; Hananiah is the LORD has been gracious and Azariah the LORD has helped, both ending in Yah. None of the new names carries the God of Israel, and Belteshazzar is named after the name of my god, the king says (4:8). The verb is va-yasem, set: twice in v7 the chief set names on them, and in v8 Daniel set it on his heart not to defile himself.

  • v8 "that he would not defile himself" — the chapter gives Daniel's resolve, not his reason. The law forbids wine only to a Nazirite (Numbers 6:3) and to priests entering the tent (Leviticus 10:9), and he refuses the king's wine as well as his food. Ezekiel had been told, This is how the sons of Israel will eat their bread unclean among the nations where I will drive them (Ezekiel 4:13).

  • vv10, 15 "downcast… fatter of flesh" — words from Joseph's story. Zo'afim, downcast, is what Joseph saw in Pharaoh's two officers, sarisim, in prison (Genesis 40:6–7), and the Greek here has skythrōpa, the word of Joseph's question, Why are your faces bad today? (Genesis 40:7). Beri'ei basar, fat of flesh, is said of Pharaoh's seven good cows, beautiful of appearance and fat of flesh (Genesis 41:2).

  • v20 "the magicians and enchanters" — chartummim, the magicians of Egypt, who could not interpret Pharaoh's dream (Genesis 41:8, 24; Exodus 7:11). Ashshafim, enchanters, is a word found only in Daniel. Ten times is eser yadot, ten hands, as Benjamin's portion was five times more, chamesh yadot (Genesis 43:34).

  • v21 "until the first year of King Cyrus" — the year of the decree that sent the exiles home (Ezra 1:1). Daniel's service spans the whole exile. The verse does not mark his death: a vision in 10:1 is dated to the third year of Cyrus.

chapters.title: The Statue and the Stone
chapters.html:
Daniel 2

The King's Dream

1In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams; his spirit was beaten, and his sleep left him.

2The king ordered that the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers and the Chaldeans be called to tell the king his dreams. They came and stood before the king.

3The king said to them, "I have had a dream, and my spirit is beaten with wanting to know the dream."

4The Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: "O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will tell the interpretation."

5The king answered the Chaldeans, "My word is firm: if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be torn limb from limb, and your houses will be made a dunghill.

6But if you tell the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation."

7They answered a second time, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will tell its interpretation."

8The king answered, "I know for certain that you are trying to gain time, because you see that my word is firm:

9if you do not make the dream known to me, there is one sentence for you. You have agreed among yourselves to speak lying and corrupt words before me until the time changes. So tell me the dream, and I will know that you can tell me its interpretation."

10The Chaldeans answered the king, "There is no man on earth who can tell the king's matter, because no king, however great and powerful, has asked such a thing of any magician or enchanter or Chaldean.

11What the king asks is too hard, and there is no one else who can tell it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh."

12At this the king became angry and very furious, and he ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be destroyed.

13The decree went out, and the wise men were to be killed; and they looked for Daniel and his companions to kill them.

14Then Daniel spoke with prudence and tact to Arioch, the king's chief of the slaughterers, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.

15He said to Arioch, the king's officer, "Why is the decree from the king so harsh?" Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.

16Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so that he could tell the king the interpretation.

The Mystery Revealed

17Then Daniel went to his house and made the matter known to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, his companions,

18to seek compassion from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

19Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.

20Daniel said,
"Blessed be the name of God
from everlasting to everlasting,
for wisdom and might are His.

21He changes times and seasons;
He removes kings and sets up kings;
He gives wisdom to the wise
and knowledge to those who have understanding.

22He reveals deep and hidden things;
He knows what is in the darkness,
and the light dwells with Him.

23To You, God of my fathers,
I give thanks and praise,
for You have given me wisdom and might,
and now You have made known to me what we asked of You;
You have made known to us the king's matter."

The Dream and Its Interpretation

24So Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said to him, "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will tell the king the interpretation."

25Then Arioch quickly brought Daniel in before the king and said to him, "I have found a man among the exiles of Judah who will make known the interpretation to the king."

26The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to make known to me the dream I saw and its interpretation?"

27Daniel answered the king, "No wise men, enchanters, magicians or diviners can tell the king the mystery the king has asked about.

28But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be in the end of days. Your dream and the visions of your head on your bed were these:

29As for you, O king, on your bed your thoughts turned to what would be after this, and He who reveals mysteries has made known to you what will be.

30As for me, this mystery has been revealed to me not because of any wisdom in me more than in anyone living, but so that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and you may know the thoughts of your heart.

31"You were watching, O king, and you saw a statue, one great statue. That statue was huge and its brightness extraordinary; it stood in front of you, and its appearance was terrifying.

32The head of that statue was of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,

33its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.

34You watched while a stone was cut out, not by hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them.

35Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were crushed all together and became like chaff from the summer threshing floors; the wind carried them away, and not a trace of them was found. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.

36"This was the dream, and we will tell the king its interpretation.

37You, O king, are the king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the might and the glory.

38Wherever they live, the sons of men, the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens, He has given them into your hand and made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.

39After you another kingdom will arise, lower than yours, and then a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.

40A fourth kingdom will be strong as iron. Just as iron crushes and shatters everything, like iron that smashes, it will crush and smash all these.

41As you saw the feet and the toes, partly of potter's clay and partly of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but some of the firmness of iron will be in it, just as you saw the iron mixed with the soft clay.

42As the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, part of the kingdom will be strong and part of it brittle.

43As you saw the iron mixed with soft clay, they will mix with one another by the seed of men, but they will not hold together, one with the other, just as iron does not mix with clay.

44In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and the kingdom will not be left to another people. It will crush all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, and it will stand forever,

45just as you saw that a stone was cut from the mountain, not by hands, and that it crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold. A great God has made known to the king what will be after this. The dream is certain, and its interpretation trustworthy."

The King Bows Down

46Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and worshipped Daniel, and he ordered that an offering and soothing aromas be offered to him.

47The king said to Daniel, "Truly your God is God of gods and Lord of kings, and a revealer of mysteries, since you have been able to reveal this mystery."

48Then the king made Daniel great and gave him many great gifts. He made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.

49At Daniel's request the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained at the king's gate.

Notes

  • v1 "In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar" — the four were to be trained for three years before they stood before the king (1:5, 18), and here, in the king's second year, Daniel is already counted among the wise men (v13). The book does not set the two dates side by side or explain how they fit.

  • vv1–3, 10–11 Pharaoh's dream again — va-tippa'em ruchi, my spirit is beaten (v3), is letter for letter what is said of Pharaoh, his spirit was beaten (Genesis 41:8). The magicians cannot answer, as Egypt's could not: there is no one to interpret it (Genesis 41:15). Then a young man from among the exiles is brought in, says the wisdom is not his own (v30), as Joseph said Not I. God will answer (Genesis 41:16), and is set over the province (v48), as Joseph was over all the land of Egypt (Genesis 41:41). Arioch is chief of the slaughterers, the title of Potiphar (Genesis 37:36).

  • v4 "in Aramaic" — aramit, and from the next words the book itself is in Aramaic, through 7:28; it returns to Hebrew in chapter 8. The same word stands before the Aramaic of Ezra: The letter was written in Aramaic (Ezra 4:7).

  • vv5, 8 "My word is firm" — millta minni azda. Azda is found only in these two verses, and it is read as settled, certain: the king has given his word and will not take it back. In v9 he gives the reason: tell me the dream, and I will know that you can tell me its interpretation. The Greek reads the word has gone from me, that is, the king has forgotten the dream. Choice in the report.

  • vv11, 27–28 "the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh… a God in heaven who reveals mysteries" — the Chaldeans say only gods could tell the dream, and gods do not live among mortals. Daniel's answer is a God who does tell it. Raz, mystery, a secret that is made known, comes eight times in the chapter; the Greek is mystērion, the word of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 13:11).

  • v28 "in the end of days" — be-acharit yomayya, the Aramaic of Jacob's words to his sons, I will tell you what will befall you in the end of days (Genesis 49:1), and of Balaam's (Numbers 24:14). In v29 the same thing is what would be after this.

  • vv34–35, 45 the stone — cut out, not by hands: no one quarries it. It was cut from the mountain (v45), and it became a great mountain and filled the whole earth (v35). It strikes the statue at its weakest part, the feet, and all the metals fall together. The Greek has from a mountain already in v34.

  • vv37–38 "the king of kings… the beasts of the field" — Ezekiel gives Nebuchadnezzar the same title (Ezekiel 26:7), and Jeremiah the same grant: I have given him even the beasts of the field to serve him (Jeremiah 27:6). The head of gold is told that his kingdom was given to him.

  • v43 "they will mix with one another by the seed of men" — mit'arvin lehevon bi-zra anasha. Seed is offspring, so the mixing may be by marriage between peoples or royal houses; the verse says no more than that. Davqin, hold together, is the Aramaic of cling: iron and clay can be pressed together, but they do not cling.

  • vv46–47 "an offering and soothing aromas… God of gods" — minchah ve-nichochin, the words of the altar; Ezra has nichochin for what is offered to the God of heaven, sacrifices of soothing aroma (Ezra 6:10). The king offers them to Daniel, then calls Daniel's God God of gods and Lord of kings, the words of Moses with one changed: God of gods and Lord of lords (Deuteronomy 10:17).

chapters.title: The Statue of Gold, and the Fourth Man in the Fire
chapters.html:
Daniel 3

The Statue of Gold

1King Nebuchadnezzar made a statue of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.

2Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent to gather the satraps, the prefects and the governors, the counselors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates and all the officials of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

3Then the satraps, the prefects and the governors, the counselors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates and all the officials of the provinces gathered for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before the statue that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

4The herald called out loudly, "You are commanded, peoples, nations and languages:

5when you hear the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the lyre, the harp, the pipes and every kind of music, you are to fall down and worship the statue of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.

6Whoever does not fall down and worship will at that very moment be thrown into the burning fiery furnace."

7So at that time, as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the lyre, the harp and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations and languages fell down and worshipped the statue of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

The Accusation

8At that time certain Chaldeans came forward and denounced the Jews.

9They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "O king, live forever!

10You, O king, have made a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, the flute, the zither, the lyre, the harp, the pipes and every kind of music shall fall down and worship the statue of gold,

11and whoever does not fall down and worship shall be thrown into the burning fiery furnace.

12There are certain Jews whom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. These men pay no attention to you, O king. They do not serve your gods, and they do not worship the statue of gold that you have set up."

13Then Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and fury, ordered Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego to be brought, and these men were brought before the king.

14Nebuchadnezzar said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the statue of gold that I have set up?

30Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the province of Babylon.

  • v1 "a statue of gold" — tselem, the word for the statue of the dream (2:31–35), where only the head was gold and the head was Nebuchadnezzar (2:38). This statue is gold from head to foot. The Greek dates it in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

  • vv2–15 the lists, again and again — the chapter repeats itself: the eight ranks of officials twice (vv2–3), the six instruments four times (vv5, 7, 10, 15), the statue… that Nebuchadnezzar set up eight times, the burning fiery furnace eight times. Three of the instruments have Greek names: qatros is kitharis, the zither; pesanterin is psaltērion, the harp; sumponyah is symphōnia, the pipes. All three are found only in this chapter.

  • v8 "denounced the Jews" — akhalu qartseihon di Yehudaye, ate the pieces of the Jews, the Aramaic way of saying slander. The same words are used of the men who accuse Daniel (6:24).

  • vv15–18 "If our God whom we serve is able… But if not" — the friends answer in the shape of the king's own sentence. He said if you are ready (hen itheikhon atidin)… but if you do not (ve-hen la); they say if our God… is able (hen itai Elahana… yakhil)… but if not (ve-hen la). Itai with a verb is is doing it, as in Are you able (2:26) and you do not serve (v14). He asked who is the god who will rescue you from my hands?, and they answer that their refusal does not depend on the answer. The accents of the Hebrew text pause after hen itai, which reads If it is so, our God… is able; the Greek has For there is a God whom we serve, able to rescue us. Choice in the report.

  • v19 "the look of his face changed" — tselem anpohi, the image of his face: the statue's word, now used of the king's own face. Shena, change, comes three times: his face changed (v19), their cloaks were not changed (v27), and they changed the king's word, here set the king's word aside (v28).

  • v21 "their cloaks, their tunics, their hats" — rare words. Sarbal is found only here and in v27, and pattish only here; karbela is related to the verb of David clothed in a robe of fine linen (1 Chronicles 15:27). What each garment was is uncertain. The Greek has sarabara, tiaras and leg coverings.

  • v23 the Greek addition — at this point the Greek has sixty-seven verses the Aramaic does not: the three walking in the flame and praising God; the prayer of Azariah, we have sinned and transgressed; the furnace fed with naphtha, pitch, tow and brush until the flame streams forty-nine cubits above it and burns the Chaldeans near it; the angel of the Lord coming down into the furnace and making its middle like a whistling wind of dew; and the song of the three, Blessed are You, Lord, God of our fathers, calling on all creation to bless the Lord. The Greek then goes on with v24, the king hearing them sing.

  • v25 "like a son of the gods" — bar elahin. Elahin is the plural the king and the Chaldeans use for gods (2:11, 47; 3:14), and in v28 the king himself names the fourth: His messenger. The Greek has a son of God. Choice in the report.

  • v27 "the smell of fire was not on them" — Isaiah's promise in the event: when you walk through fire, you will not be burned, and the flame will not consume you (Isaiah 43:2). The fire that did not singe their hair killed the men who threw them in (v22).

chapters.title: The Tree Cut Down, and the King Who Ate Grass
chapters.html:
Daniel 4

The King's Letter

1King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, nations and languages who live in all the earth: May your peace be great!

2It has seemed good to me to tell the signs and wonders that the Most High God has done for me.

3How great are His signs,
and how mighty His wonders!
His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom,
and His dominion is from generation to generation.

The Dream of the Tree

4I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.

5I saw a dream, and it made me afraid; the thoughts on my bed and the visions of my head alarmed me.

6So I made a decree that all the wise men of Babylon be brought in before me, so that they might make known to me the interpretation of the dream.

7Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans and the diviners came in, and I told them the dream, but they could not make its interpretation known to me.

8At last Daniel came in before me, whose name is Belteshazzar after the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and I told him the dream:

9"Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and no mystery is too hard for you. Tell me the visions of my dream that I saw, and its interpretation.

10These were the visions of my head on my bed: I was looking, and there was a tree in the middle of the earth, and its height was great.

11The tree grew and became strong; its top reached to heaven, and it could be seen to the end of the whole earth.

12Its leaves were beautiful and its fruit abundant, and on it was food for all. Under it the beasts of the field found shade, and the birds of the heavens lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.

13I was looking in the visions of my head on my bed, and a watcher, a holy one, came down from heaven.

14He called out loudly and said this: 'Cut down the tree and cut off its branches, strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the beasts flee from under it and the birds from its branches.

15But leave the stump of its roots in the earth, in a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be wet with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts in the grass of the earth.

16Let his heart be changed from a man's, and let a beast's heart be given to him, and let seven times pass over him.

17The sentence is by the decree of the watchers, and the decision by the word of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men and gives it to whom He will, and sets over it the lowliest of men.'

18This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom can make known to me the interpretation; but you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you."

The Interpretation

19Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was appalled for a while, and his thoughts alarmed him. The king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation alarm you." Belteshazzar answered, "My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!

20The tree that you saw, which grew and became strong, whose top reached to heaven and which could be seen in all the earth,

21whose leaves were beautiful and its fruit abundant, and on which was food for all, under which the beasts of the field lived and in whose branches the birds of the heavens dwelt —

22it is you, O king, who have grown and become strong. Your greatness has grown and reached to heaven, and your dominion to the end of the earth.

23As for the king seeing a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump of its roots in the earth, in a band of iron and bronze, in the grass of the field; let him be wet with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts of the field, until seven times pass over him' —

24this is the interpretation, O king, and it is the decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:

25you will be driven from among men, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field. You will be made to eat grass like oxen, and you will be wet with the dew of heaven, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men and gives it to whom He will.

26As it was commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree, your kingdom will be restored to you from the time you know that Heaven rules.

27Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you: break off your sins by doing what is right, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps your ease will be prolonged."

Seven Times

28All this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.

29At the end of twelve months he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon.

30The king said, "Is this not great Babylon, which I have built as a royal house by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?"

31While the word was still in the king's mouth, a voice fell from heaven: "To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has departed from you.

32You will be driven from among men, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field. You will be made to eat grass like oxen, and seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men and gives it to whom He will."

33At that very moment the word was fulfilled on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from among men and ate grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.

The King Praises the King of Heaven

34At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me. I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored Him who lives forever,
for His dominion is an everlasting dominion,
and His kingdom is from generation to generation.

35All the inhabitants of the earth are counted as nothing,
and He does as He wills with the host of heaven
and with the inhabitants of the earth.
No one can hold back His hand
or say to Him, "What have You done?"

36At that very time my understanding returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom my majesty and my splendor returned to me. My counselors and my lords sought me out, and I was established again in my kingdom, and still more greatness was added to me.

37Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and honor the King of heaven, for all His works are truth and His ways are justice, and He is able to humble those who walk in pride.

Notes

  • vv1–3 the king's letter — in the Hebrew text these three verses end chapter 3 (3:31–33), and v4 here is its 4:1; the English numbering is followed. The chapter is Nebuchadnezzar's own letter: he says I while he tells the dream (vv4–18), the story speaks of him from outside while he is mad (vv28–33), and he says I again when his understanding returns (v34). His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom (v3) is the psalm's Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom (Psalm 145:13), in a Babylonian king's mouth.

  • v4 "at ease… flourishing" — shelē, at ease, is the root of Daniel's last words to him, perhaps your ease (shelevah) will be prolonged (v27). Ra'nan, flourishing, is the word for a green, leafy tree, as in under every leafy tree (Deuteronomy 12:2). The king describes himself as a tree before he dreams of one.

  • vv8–9, 18 "the spirit of the holy gods" — ruach elahin qaddishin. Elahin is plural, and so is holy. The plural is the book's word for gods (2:11, 47; 3:14), and in the same breath the king names my god (v8). Hebrew can put a plural adjective with the one God: He is a holy God is Elohim qedoshim, holy plural (Joshua 24:19). The Greek has the holy Spirit of God. Choice in the report.

  • vv10–12, 20–22 the tree — Ezekiel's cedar: In its boughs all the birds of the heavens made their nests; under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth (Ezekiel 31:6), cut down because it grew proud of its height (Ezekiel 31:10–12). Jesus' mustard seed grows into a tree so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches (Matthew 13:32).

  • vv13, 17, 23 "a watcher, a holy one" — ir, from the root for being awake, found only in this chapter. The Greek does not translate it; it writes eir. 1 Enoch's name for the angels who came down to earth is the Watchers (1 Enoch 1:5).

  • vv16, 23, 25, 32 "seven times" — shiv'ah iddanin. Iddan is the word of 2:21, He changes times and seasons, and the chapter does not say how long a time is. The Old Greek, the second Greek version of Daniel, has seven years.

  • vv17, 25, 32 "the Most High rules over the kingdom of men" — the sentence is said three times, by the watcher, by Daniel and by the voice from heaven, and the third time it is done. The lowliest of men (v17) is shefal, the verb of the king's last words: He is able to humble (hashpalah) those who walk in pride (v37). In v26 the same truth is Heaven rules: Heaven stands for God, as in the question The baptism of John — where was it from? From heaven, or from men? (Matthew 21:25).

  • v27 "break off your sins by doing what is right" — chatayakh be-tsidqah feruq. Tsidqah is the Aramaic of tsedaqah, righteousness, found in the Bible's Aramaic only here; peruq is break off, or redeem. The second half names the poor, your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. The Greek reads both halves as giving to the poor: redeem your sins by almsgiving. Choice in the report.

  • v35 "What have You done?" — Job asked it of God, Who will say to Him, "What are You doing?" (Job 9:12), and Ecclesiastes of a king, who may say to him, "What are you doing?" (Ecclesiastes 8:4). Here a king says it of God. Counted as nothing is Isaiah's word for the nations, counted by Him as less than nothing (Isaiah 40:17).

chapters.title: The Writing on the Wall
chapters.html:
Daniel 5

Belshazzar's Feast

1King Belshazzar made a great feast for a thousand of his lords, and he drank wine in front of the thousand.

2As he tasted the wine, Belshazzar ordered that the vessels of gold and silver that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem be brought, so that the king and his lords, his wives and his secondary wives might drink from them.

3Then they brought the vessels of gold that had been taken out of the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king and his lords, his wives and his secondary wives drank from them.

4They drank wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.

The Hand

5At that very moment the fingers of a human hand came out and wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace, and the king watched the hand as it wrote.

6Then the king's color changed, and his thoughts alarmed him; the joints of his hips came loose, and his knees knocked together.

7The king cried out loudly for the enchanters, the Chaldeans and the diviners to be brought in. The king said to the wise men of Babylon, "Whoever reads this writing and tells me its interpretation will be clothed in purple, with a chain of gold around his neck, and will rule as third in the kingdom."

8Then all the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or make known its interpretation to the king.

9Then King Belshazzar was greatly alarmed, his color changed, and his lords were bewildered.

10Because of the words of the king and his lords, the queen entered the banquet hall. The queen said, "O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts alarm you or your color change.

11There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. In the days of your father, light and insight and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him, and King Nebuchadnezzar your father, your father the king, made him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans and diviners,

12because an excellent spirit, knowledge and insight to interpret dreams, explain riddles and untie knots were found in this Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will tell the interpretation."

Daniel Before the King

25This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.

27TEKEL — you have been weighed in the balances and found wanting.

  • vv2–4 "the vessels… the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone" — the vessels Nebuchadnezzar put in the treasure house of his god (1:2) are brought out for a drinking party, and the drinkers praise gods made of the statue's metals (2:32–33), with wood and stone added.   • vv6, 12, 16 "the joints of his hips came loose… untie knots" — qitrei charseh mishtarayin, the knots of his loins were untied (v6).   • v11 "the spirit of the holy gods" — the words of 4:8, 9, 18, now in the queen's mouth, and in v14 the spirit of the gods. The Greek has the Spirit of God in both verses. Choice in the report on chapter 4.

  • vv19–22 "he brought low… you have not humbled your heart" — shefal, the verb Nebuchadnezzar's letter ended with, He is able to humble those who walk in pride (4:37).   • v21 "with the wild donkeys" — a detail chapter 4 does not have. There the king's dwelling was with the beasts of the field (4:25, 32).

  • v23 "which do not see or hear or know… the God in whose hand is your breath" — the law's description of the gods of exile, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell (Deuteronomy 4:28). Nishmah, breath, is the Aramaic of the breath God blew into the first human, the breath of lives (Genesis 2:7).

  • vv25–28 MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN — three words that are weights: mene is the mina (Ezekiel 45:12), teqel is the Aramaic of shekel, and peres is from the verb divide.   • vv30–31 "That very night… Darius the Mede" — the night of the feast. In the Hebrew text v31 is 6:1; the English numbering is followed. Darius the Mede is found only in Daniel (here and 11:1; 9:1 makes him a Mede by descent); the Darius of Ezra is king of Persia (Ezra 4:24).

chapters.title: Daniel in the Den of Lions
chapters.html:
Daniel 6

The Plot

1It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom a hundred and twenty satraps, to be throughout the whole kingdom,

2and over them three administrators, of whom Daniel was one, so that these satraps would give account to them and the king would suffer no loss.

3Then this Daniel distinguished himself above the administrators and the satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.

4Then the administrators and the satraps looked for a charge to find against Daniel in the affairs of the kingdom, but they could find no charge or fault, because he was faithful, and no negligence or fault was found in him.

5Then these men said, "We will not find any charge against this Daniel unless we find it against him in the law of his God."

6Then these administrators and satraps came thronging to the king and said to him, "King Darius, live forever!

7All the administrators of the kingdom, the prefects and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, have agreed that the king should establish a statute and enforce an injunction: whoever makes a petition to any god or man for thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be thrown into the den of lions.

8Now, O king, establish the injunction and sign the document, so that it cannot be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot pass away."

9So King Darius signed the document and the injunction.

Daniel's Prayer

10When Daniel knew that the document had been signed, he went to his house. In its upper room he had windows open toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he knelt on his knees and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as he had done before.

11Then these men came thronging and found Daniel making petition and pleading before his God.

12Then they came near and spoke before the king about the king's injunction: "Did you not sign an injunction that anyone who makes a petition to any god or man for thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be thrown into the den of lions?" The king answered, "The thing stands firm, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot pass away."

13Then they answered before the king, "Daniel, who is one of the exiles of Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the injunction you have signed, but three times a day he makes his petition."

14When the king heard these words, he was greatly distressed, and he set his mind on Daniel to rescue him; until the sun went down he labored to save him.

15Then these men came thronging to the king and said to the king, "Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians that no injunction or statute that the king establishes can be changed."

The Den

16Then the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king said to Daniel, "Your God, whom you serve continually, He will rescue you!"

17A stone was brought and laid on the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the signet rings of his lords, so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.

18Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting; no diversions were brought before him, and his sleep fled from him.

19At dawn, at first light, the king rose and went in haste to the den of lions.

20As he came near the den, he cried out to Daniel in an anguished voice. The king said to Daniel, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?"

21Then Daniel spoke with the king: "O king, live forever!

22My God sent His messenger and shut the mouths of the lions, and they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before Him; and before you too, O king, I have done no harm."

23Then the king was very glad, and he ordered that Daniel be taken up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

24The king gave the order, and those men who had denounced Daniel were brought and thrown into the den of lions, they, their sons and their wives; and before they reached the bottom of the den the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.

The King's Decree

25Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, nations and languages who live in all the earth: "May your peace be great!

26I make a decree that in all the dominion of my kingdom people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel,
for He is the living God,
and He endures forever;
His kingdom shall never be destroyed,
and His dominion shall be to the end.

27He rescues and saves;
He does signs and wonders
in heaven and on earth,
He who has rescued Daniel
from the power of the lions."

28So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

Notes

  • v1 the numbering — in the Hebrew text chapter 6 begins one verse earlier, with Darius the Mede received the kingdom (5:31 here), so English 6:1–28 is Hebrew 6:2–29. The English numbering is followed.

  • vv4, 23 "he was faithful… he had trusted in his God" — mehemin and heimin, one root. Daniel is found to be faithful to the king, so no fault can be found, and he comes out of the den unharmed because he had trusted in his God. In 2:45 the same root made the interpretation trustworthy.

  • vv6, 11, 15 "came thronging" — hargishu, three times, each time as a body. The verb in Hebrew is found only in Why do the nations rage (ragshu, Psalm 2:1), where the nations and their rulers set themselves against the LORD.

  • v7 "All the administrators of the kingdom… have agreed" — there were three administrators, of whom Daniel was one (v2). The plotters tell the king that all of them agree, and the one left out is the man the law is made to catch.

  • vv8, 12, 15 "the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot pass away" — Esther's court has the same law: let it be written among the laws of Persia and Media so that it may not pass away (Esther 1:19), and a writing written in the king's name and sealed with the king's signet ring cannot be revoked (Esther 8:8). The king is caught by his own signature.

  • v10 "windows open toward Jerusalem… three times a day" — Solomon's prayer had asked God to hear the exiles when they pray to You toward their land… the city that You have chosen and the house that I have built for Your name (1 Kings 8:48). The psalm prays three times: Evening and morning and at noon I complain and moan, and He hears my voice (Psalm 55:17).

  • vv17–18 the stone and the night — a stone on the mouth of the den, sealed so that nothing might be changed, as the tomb was made secure sealing the stone (Matthew 27:66). Dachavan, diversions, is found only in v18, and what it was is uncertain; the Greek has food. The Greek also adds to v18: and God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm Daniel.

  • vv20, 26 "the living God" — Elaha chayya, the God David named against Goliath, the ranks of the living God (1 Samuel 17:26), and Hezekiah against Assyria, to defy the living God (2 Kings 19:4). Here a Persian king names Him twice.

  • vv22–23 "they have not harmed me… I have done no harm… no harm was found on him" — chabal, three times: the lions did not harm him, he did the king no harm, and no harm was found on him, as no harm was found on the three in the fire (3:25). Hebrews names the shutting of lions' mouths among the deeds of faith (Hebrews 11:33).

chapters.title: The Four Beasts, and One Like a Son of Man
chapters.html:
Daniel 7

The Four Beasts

1In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head on his bed. Then he wrote down the dream and told the sum of the matter.

2Daniel said, "I was looking in my vision by night, and the four winds of heaven were stirring up the great sea.

3Four great beasts came up out of the sea, each different from the other.

4The first was like a lion and had eagle's wings. I watched until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a man, and a man's heart was given to it.

5Another beast, a second one, was like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth; and it was told, 'Arise, devour much flesh!'

6After this I was looking, and there was another, like a leopard, with four wings of a bird on its back. The beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.

7After this I was looking in the visions of the night, and there was a fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful and exceedingly strong. It had great iron teeth; it devoured and crushed, and trampled what was left with its feet. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

8I was considering the horns, and another horn, a little one, came up among them, and three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots before it. This horn had eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.

The Ancient of Days

9I was looking
until thrones were set in place,
and the Ancient of Days took His seat.
His clothing was white as snow,
and the hair of His head like pure wool;
His throne was flames of fire,
its wheels burning fire.

10A river of fire
was flowing and coming out from before Him;
a thousand thousands served Him,
and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him.
The court sat,
and the books were opened.

11I was looking then because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking. I was looking until the beast was killed, and its body destroyed and given to the burning fire.

12As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away, but their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.

13I was looking in the visions of the night,
and with the clouds of heaven
there came one like a son of man;
he came to the Ancient of Days
and was brought near before Him.

14To him was given dominion,
glory and a kingdom,
that all peoples, nations and languages
should serve him.
His dominion is an everlasting dominion
that will not pass away,
and his kingdom one
that will not be destroyed.

The Interpretation

15As for me, Daniel, my spirit within me was distressed, and the visions of my head alarmed me.

16I approached one of those who stood there and asked him the truth about all this. So he told me and made known to me the interpretation of the matters:

17'These great beasts, which are four, are four kings who will arise from the earth.

18But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess the kingdom forever, forever and ever.'

19Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others, exceedingly terrifying, with teeth of iron and claws of bronze, which devoured and crushed and trampled what was left with its feet;

20and about the ten horns on its head, and the other horn which came up and before which three fell — the horn that had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and that looked greater than its fellows.

21I was looking, and that horn made war with the holy ones and prevailed over them,

22until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given to the holy ones of the Most High, and the time came, and the holy ones possessed the kingdom.

23This is what he said: 'The fourth beast shall be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms; it will devour the whole earth, trample it down and crush it.

24As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them; he will be different from the former ones and will bring low three kings.

25He will speak words against the Most High and wear out the holy ones of the Most High, and he will intend to change times and law; and they will be given into his hand for a time, times and half a time.

26But the court will sit, and his dominion will be taken away, to be consumed and destroyed to the end.

27The kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. Their kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey them.'

28Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly alarmed me, and my color changed; but I kept the matter in my heart."

Notes

  • v1 "In the first year of Belshazzar" — the book steps back in time, before the feast of chapter 5, and from here to the end Daniel tells his own visions. The Aramaic runs to v28; the book returns to Hebrew at 8:1.

  • vv3–7 four beasts — four kingdoms again, as the four metals of the statue were (2:37–40): here four kings who will arise from the earth (v17), though the beasts come up out of the sea. The first is given a man's heart (v4), where Nebuchadnezzar heard let a beast's heart be given to him (4:16).

  • vv9–10 the Ancient of Days — attiq yomin, one advanced in days. Ezekiel saw a throne with wheels and fire all around the one seated on it (Ezekiel 1:15, 26–27); 1 Enoch saw streams of flaming fire from beneath the throne and ten thousand times ten thousand before Him (1 Enoch 14:19, 22). The books were opened is also in Revelation (Revelation 20:12).

  • vv13–14 "one like a son of man" — ke-var enash. Bar enash is ordinary Aramaic for a human being: after four beasts out of the sea comes one like a human, with the clouds of heaven. 1 Enoch takes up the picture: One who had a head of days… With Him was another, whose face had the appearance of a man (1 Enoch 46:1). Jesus answered the high priest with this verse: you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of heaven (Matthew 26:64). The Old Greek reads and he was there as the Ancient of Days.

  • v14 "should serve him" — yiflechun, the verb of serving God in chapters 3 and 6: the three would not serve the king's gods (3:12, 18), and Darius called Daniel's God the one whom you serve continually (6:16, 20). Here all peoples serve the one like a son of man. Will not pass away is the verb of the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot pass away (6:8).

  • vv18, 21–22, 27 "the holy ones of the Most High" — in chapter 4 the holy ones are heavenly beings, the watcher who comes down (4:13, 17). Here the holy ones are warred against and worn out (vv21, 25), and in v27 the kingdom goes to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. Judgment was given to the holy ones (v22) can mean that judgment was given in their favor or that they were given the right to judge; the Aramaic, dina yehiv le-, allows both.

  • v25 "change times and law… a time, times and half a time" — zimnin ve-dat. Changing times is what Daniel said God does: He changes times and seasons; He removes kings and sets up kings (2:21). Iddan, time, is the word of the king's seven times (4:16); here it is one, two and a half. Revelation uses the same measure (Revelation 12:14).

  • v27 "Their kingdom… serve and obey them" — the Aramaic is singular, malkhuteh… leh, its kingdom… serve and obey it (or him). It can point to the people, spoken of as one, or to the Most High. Choice in the report.

  • v28 "I kept the matter in my heart" — in the Greek, to rhēma en tē kardia mou dietērēsa, the words used of Jacob after Joseph's dreams, his father kept it in mind (Genesis 37:11, dietērēsen to rhēma), and of Mary in Luke (Luke 2:51).

Daniel said, "I was looking in my vision by night, and the four winds of heaven were stirring up the great sea.
Four great beasts came up out of the sea, each different from the other.

The first was like a lion and had eagle's wings. I watched until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a man, and a man's heart was given to it.
Another beast, a second one, was like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth; and it was told, 'Arise, devour much flesh!'
After this I was looking, and there was another, like a leopard, with four wings of a bird on its back. The beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.

After this I was looking in the visions of the night, and there was a fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful and exceedingly strong. It had great iron teeth; it devoured and crushed, and trampled what was left with its feet. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

I was considering the horns, and another horn, a little one, came up among them, and three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots before it. This horn had eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.
The Ancient of Days

I was looking until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took His seat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool; His throne was flames of fire, its wheels burning fire.
A river of fire was flowing and coming out from before Him; a thousand thousands served Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him. The court sat, and the books were opened.
I was looking then because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking. I was looking until the beast was killed, and its body destroyed and given to the burning fire.
As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away, but their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
I was looking in the visions of the night, and with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man; he came to the Ancient of Days and was brought near before Him.

To him was given dominion, glory and a kingdom, that all peoples, nations and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom one that will not be destroyed.
The Interpretation
As for me, Daniel, my spirit within me was distressed, and the visions of my head alarmed me.
I approached one of those who stood there and asked him the truth about all this. So he told me and made known to me the interpretation of the matters:
'These great beasts, which are four, are four kings who will arise from the earth.
But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess the kingdom forever, forever and ever.'

Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others, exceedingly terrifying, with teeth of iron and claws of bronze, which devoured and crushed and trampled what was left with its feet;
and about the ten horns on its head, and the other horn which came up and before which three fell — the horn that had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and that looked greater than its fellows.
I was looking, and that horn made war with the holy ones and prevailed over them,
until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given to the holy ones of the Most High, and the time came, and the holy ones possessed the kingdom.
This is what he said: 'The fourth beast shall be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms; it will devour the whole earth, trample it down and crush it.
As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them; he will be different from the former ones and will bring low three kings.

He will speak words against the Most High and wear out the holy ones of the Most High, and he will intend to change times and law; and they will be given into his hand for a time, times and half a time.
But the court will sit, and his dominion will be taken away, to be consumed and destroyed to the end.

The kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. Their kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey them.'
Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly alarmed me, and my color changed; but I kept the matter in my heart."

chapters.title: The Ram and the Goat
chapters.html:
Daniel 8

The Vision

1In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that had appeared to me at first.

2I saw in the vision, and as I watched I was in Susa the citadel, in the province of Elam; I saw in the vision, and I was by the Ulai canal.

3I lifted my eyes and saw a ram standing in front of the canal. It had two horns; both horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last.

4I saw the ram charging west and north and south. No beast could stand before it, and no one could rescue from its power. It did as it pleased and made itself great.

5As I was considering, a male goat came from the west across the face of the whole earth without touching the ground, and the goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.

6It came to the ram with the two horns, which I had seen standing in front of the canal, and ran at it in the fury of its strength.

7I saw it reach the ram. It was enraged against it and struck the ram and broke its two horns, and the ram had no strength to stand before it. It threw the ram down to the ground and trampled on it, and no one could rescue the ram from its power.

8The male goat made itself exceedingly great; but when it was strong, the great horn was broken, and in its place came up four conspicuous horns toward the four winds of heaven.

9Out of one of them came a horn, starting small, which grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the beautiful land.

10It grew great, up to the host of heaven, and it threw some of the host and some of the stars down to the earth and trampled on them.

11It made itself great even up to the Prince of the host; the continual offering was taken away from Him, and the place of His sanctuary was thrown down.

12A host will be given over, together with the continual offering, because of transgression; it will throw truth to the ground, and it will act and prosper.

13Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to the one who was speaking, "How long is the vision — the continual offering, the transgression that desolates, and the giving over of both the sanctuary and the host to be trampled?"

14He said to me, "For two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be set right."

Gabriel Explains

15When I, Daniel, had seen the vision and was seeking to understand it, there stood before me one who looked like a man.

16I heard a human voice between the banks of the Ulai, which called out, "Gabriel, make this man understand the vision."

17He came near where I stood, and when he came I was terrified and fell on my face. He said to me, "Understand, son of man, that the vision is for the time of the end."

18While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground; but he touched me and set me on my feet.

19He said, "I am about to make known to you what will happen in the last part of the wrath, for it concerns the appointed time of the end.

20The ram you saw with the two horns — they are the kings of Media and Persia.

21The shaggy male goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.

22As for the horn that was broken, and the four that stood up in its place: four kingdoms will stand up from his nation, but not with his power.

23At the latter end of their rule, when the transgressors have reached their full measure, a king will arise, hard of face and skilled in riddles.

24His power will be mighty, but not by his own power. He will cause astonishing destruction, and he will succeed in what he does; he will destroy mighty men and the people of the holy ones.

25By his cunning he will make deceit prosper under his hand, and in his heart he will make himself great; while they are at ease he will destroy many. He will even stand up against the Prince of princes, but he will be broken, and not by any hand.

26The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been told is true. But you, seal up the vision, for it refers to many days from now."

27I, Daniel, was overcome and lay sick for days. Then I rose and did the king's business. I was appalled by the vision, and no one understood it.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "In the third year… in Susa the citadel" — the book returns to Hebrew here and stays in it to the end. Susa is the city where Esther's story takes place, Susa the citadel (Esther 1:2). Uval, canal, is found only in this chapter.

  • vv20–21 "Media and Persia… Greece" — this time the kingdoms are named. Yavan, Greece, is Javan son of Japheth (Genesis 10:2), and Madai, Media, is his brother. The two horns of the ram are one kingdom of two peoples, the higher coming up last (v3).

  • v9 "the beautiful land" — ha-tsevi, the beauty, used alone for the land of Israel. Ezekiel calls it the most beautiful of all lands, tsevi hi le-khol ha-aratsot (Ezekiel 20:6).

  • vv11, 25 "the Prince of the host… the Prince of princes" — sar ha-tsava, the words of the figure who met Joshua, the commander of the army of the LORD (Joshua 5:14). The sanctuary in v11 is His, and Prince of princes is built like God of gods (2:47). In chapters 10–12 sar is also the title of heavenly princes, among them Michael (10:13, 21; 12:1). Choice in the report.

  • v12 "A host will be given over… because of transgression" — the hardest verse of the chapter. Its words can be read in more than one way: the host given over with the continual offering or against it, and the transgression the people's or the horn's. Its verbs also turn from what Daniel saw to what will be. The Greek has and sin was given upon the sacrifice, and righteousness was thrown to the ground.

  • v13 "the one who was speaking… the transgression that desolates" — la-palmoni, to so-and-so, found only here: the two words peloni almoni run together, the name Boaz did not say, Turn aside, friend (Ruth 4:1). Ha-pesha shomem, the transgression that desolates, comes back as shiqquts meshomem (9:27; 11:31; 12:11), which Jesus quotes from the Greek: the abomination of desolation, spoken of through Daniel the prophet (Matthew 24:15).

  • v14 "two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings" — erev boqer, evening morning, the way the days of creation are counted: it was evening, and it was morning — day one (Genesis 1:5). The number can be read as 2,300 days, or as 2,300 of the continual offerings of v13, made morning and evening (Exodus 29:38–39), which would be 1,150 days. The Greek adds days. Nitsdaq, set right, from the root of righteous, is found only here; the Greek has cleansed.

  • vv15–18 "one who looked like a man… Gabriel… son of man" — gaver, man, and the name that follows, Gavri'el, is built on it. He calls Daniel ben adam, son of man, as God called Ezekiel (Ezekiel 2:1), and as with Ezekiel the prophet falls on his face and is set on his feet (Ezekiel 1:28; 2:2). Gabriel comes again in Luke (Luke 1:19, 26).

  • vv23–25 "hard of face and skilled in riddles… not by any hand" — az panim, the words of the curse in Deuteronomy, a nation hard of face (Deuteronomy 28:50). Riddles (chidot) were Daniel's own gift (5:12). He is broken be-efes yad, without a hand, as the stone was cut out not by hands (2:34, 45).
